## 開篇固定收益論點

8月20日美國固定收益市場收盤否定了公債回購已為長端殖利率建立持久上限的看法。2年期美國公債殖利率持平於4.19%，5年期、10年期與30年期殖利率則各上升4個基點，分別至4.39%、4.69%與5.23%。5年期以遠殖利率同步上升，使2s10s與2s30s均陡峭化4個基點，分別至50與104個基點。長債殖利率因此僅比財政部8月19日意外介入前的水準低4個基點，且1個月內上升12個基點。政策公告引發強勁的單日資金流反應；但隔日完整收盤顯示，反映在長天期債券中的財政、通膨與競爭性供給溢價並未因此消失。

反轉也改變了走勢的組成。10年期實質殖利率持穩於2.35%，10年期損益兩平通膨率則上升4個基點至2.34%。美國總統川普威脅對伊朗及其貿易夥伴展開經濟行動後，Brent上漲1.77%至$93.24，WTI上漲0.51%至$86.27。週三的漲勢完全由實質殖利率驅動，損益兩平通膨率未變；週四的賣壓則使基準天期重新反映通膨補償。財政部減少民間持有存續期間的做法仍有影響，但即使實質利率不動，油價衝擊仍可推高名目殖利率。

同日傳出的兩項政策訊號，進一步凸顯前端與長端分化。2026年無投票權的舊金山聯準銀行總裁Mary Daly認為沒有急迫理由預防性升息，並表示近期通膨與勞動數據尚未出現她所擔心的廣泛持續性。同樣無投票權的聖路易聯準銀行總裁Alberto Musalem重申，他原本會支持7月升息，並認為若不收緊政策，未來18個月通膨無法回到2%的風險較高。不過，Musalem將債市賣壓歸因於政府融資與AI相關資本需求，而非聯準會公信力流失。2年期殖利率未變，顯示雙方觀點都未迫使市場立即重定價政策利率。損益兩平通膨率上升、曲線轉陡則顯示，前端保持耐心並不能使長端免受能源、赤字或供給影響。

跨資產表現符合名目折現率上升及市場質疑行政手段壓低殖利率的情境，而非全面性融資斷裂。S&P 500下跌0.87%，Nasdaq 100下跌0.72%、連續第5天下滑，VIX上升7.52%至16.01。美元指數在前一日大跌後近乎持平於98.796，黃金期貨則上漲2.07%至$4,582.30。投資級債的存續期間承受較短天期及較低品質信用債更大的損失：LQD下跌0.48%，HYG與JNK約下跌0.19%-0.20%。美國政府20年以上債券指數下跌0.81%，長天期高評級公司債指數約下跌0.85%-0.90%。這些報酬反映存續期間與總報酬壓力，而非經實測的現券利差變動。

最具影響力的新供給資訊顯示，財政部的結構性問題不但沒有縮小，反而擴大。Broadcom正洽談一項特殊目的融資，內容包括$600億-$700億優先擔保債務、可能的$300億次順位分層，總借款最高或達$1,000億，用以資助供應Anthropic及其他客戶的AI晶片。財政部可以在邊際上調整聯邦融資的期限分布，卻無法阻止高評級科技贊助方、私募資本機構與AI客戶共同爭取同一批長期儲蓄資金。因此，8月20日收盤恢復了前一日漲勢一度打亂的主次關係：能源推動通膨成分、財政部溝通改變近期資金流，而財政與AI融資仍決定實質存續期間承受的負擔。

## 回購托底首次重測失效

即使回購計畫的市場效果消退，財政部長Scott Bessent週四仍進一步強化口頭承諾。他表示，預定9月9日開始的操作，每檔規模可能超過目前規劃的$40億，並稱還有更廣泛的工具可維持市場有序運作。他也表示，政府將於本週末或下週初宣布更加著重財政整頓，川普總統已指派Bessent與預算局局長Russ Vought負責。但這些說法並未附帶具體支出、收入或債務管理措施。因此，市場得到的是規模可能更大的介入與一項即將提出的財政倡議，卻沒有降低根本借款需求的新措施。

30年期殖利率清楚反映兩者差異。盤中一度上升7個基點至5.27%，短暫高於公告前區間，收盤則為5.23%。Bessent的談話有助縮小賣壓，顯示官方反應機制仍有戰術作用；但收盤已收復週三9個基點跌幅中的大部分。10年期殖利率同樣收在4.69%，上升4個基點。政策訊號可以引發空頭回補，並降低市場對預定操作前後淨存續期間的預期；若要維持較低的均衡殖利率，則必須更大幅調整標售供給，或在通膨、成長或財政現金流方面取得可信改善。

相較市場規模與政府融資缺口，回購金額仍然有限。財政部初步規劃的9月9日至11月4日日程，原可在10年至30年期區間最多買進$140億，因此規模加倍意味至少增加$140億需求。JPMorgan估計未來數個會計年度的融資缺口超過$3.5兆，並指出在經濟接近充分就業之際，預算赤字約占GDP 6%。公債總額已突破$40兆。Bessent主張關稅收入、經濟成長與減少詐欺可改善路徑，並稱赤字很可能已見頂。承諾中的財政方案必須把這些廣泛途徑轉化為足以改變預估現金借款的措施；否則，回購只是重新配置部分期限供給。

回購的融資方式也只是重新分配利率風險，而非將其消除。財政部通常以國庫券因應波動性融資需求，因此買回或增持較長天期的非指標券，可能伴隨額外短期發行。這可降低民間投資人目前吸收的存續期間，卻提高再融資頻率，赤字也原封不動。同時，長端殖利率的訊號意義會更複雜。官方期限管理造成30年期殖利率下降，與疲弱數據引發漲勢相比，對通膨、財政可持續性或未來名目成長所傳達的訊息並不相同。

市場反轉後，溝通成本也浮上檯面。財政部才在兩週前發布例行季度借款策略，隨後便意外更改回購規模。JPMorgan與Jefferies策略師及PGIM投資人警告，偏離規律且可預測的程序，可能提高投資人要求的期限溢價。身兼財政部借款諮詢委員會成員的PGIM共同投資長Greg Peters估計，這項公告使政府在$160億20年期公債標售中節省約$2億成本。即使20年期殖利率已下降，該次標售需求仍然平淡。若投資人對未來標售規模、回購日程及政治介入門檻更不確定，單次發行的戰術性節省可與更高的結構性溢價並存。

現券交易並未顯示市場失序至需要緊急支撐。美國公債以原始面額計的交易總額為$1.246兆，較前一交易日低9.0%；名目附息券交易額為$1.016兆，下降8.6%。20年以上券種仍有$1,379億成交，共50,919筆交易，交易商對客戶交易占面額47.2%。周轉量較週三回購驅動的激增低19.2%。這次反轉發生在活躍的雙向市場，並非交易崩潰所致。財政部所稱的流動性目的或可改善非指標券運作，但當日價格走勢反映的是市場對估值及政策持久性的分歧。

美元走勢也顯示介入效果仍有邊界。即使Citi將3個月美元指數預測由102.12下調至98.34，美元仍未延續週三0.8%的跌勢，收盤近乎持平。Citi認為，回購透過降低美國殖利率及引發金融壓抑疑慮而削弱美元，並將3個月EUR/USD預測上調至1.1750。其他投資人也認為，若當局在未改善財政公信力的情況下壓低期限殖利率，美元可能成為壓力出口。週四持穩的收盤顯示，這項傳導並非自動發生。油價上漲、美國AI相關資本流入及殖利率反彈都支撐美元。較長期而言，若反覆介入卻未兌現財政措施，風險溢價仍可能由債券轉移至外匯與黃金，而非消失。

制度張力也延伸至聯準會。主席Kevin Warsh已要求投資人以經濟數據為依據，自行形成市場價格，但財政部如今明確暗示長端殖利率並未反映基本面。若回購在通膨高於目標時大幅放寬房貸、企業及整體金融情勢，聯準會可能必須判斷，這種寬鬆是否削弱了原本希望透過市場利率達成的緊縮效果。若操作規模小到不足以影響金融情勢，則只會增加雜訊，無法改變政策需求。週四的反轉較支持後一種解讀，但已宣布的擴大版工具仍使此議題持續存在。

## 油價重啟殖利率曲線的通膨交易

能源是本日利率驅動因素中最明確的變化。Brent升至$93.24，1週漲幅擴大至7.09%；10年期損益兩平通膨率則升至2.34%，同期上升10個基點。川普表示，美國將對伊朗展開經濟戰，並承諾於週一記者會公布細節，包括向持續與德黑蘭維持經濟往來的國家、銀行及企業施壓。中國是伊朗石油最大買家，使威脅影響範圍可能超越雙邊制裁升級。截至收盤尚未公布具體措施，但執法趨嚴的可能性，已降低市場對波斯灣流量受阻後現有替代安排能維持不變的信心。

這波走勢並非先前油價衝擊的簡單重演。8月19日，10年期名目殖利率下降6個基點，因實質殖利率同幅下降，損益兩平通膨率則持平於2.30%。8月20日，實質殖利率維持2.35%，名目基準殖利率上升的4個基點全由損益兩平通膨率貢獻。前後兩日的反轉顯示，市場已把財政部的存續期間介入與實體通膨傳導分開看待。回購可從交易商庫存或投資人組合中移除部分長債，卻無法創造原油供給、降低航運保險成本或解決美國與伊朗衝突。

通膨走勢仍屬受控，尚未形成系統性壓力。2年期殖利率未升、美元指數持穩，VIX收在16.01，未顯示廣泛融資壓力。WTI僅上漲0.51%，遠小於Brent漲幅，說明這是地理分布不均的衝擊，而非所有原油基準全面飆升。TIPS交易確實轉趨活躍：以面額計有$367億轉手，較前一日增加25.7%，其中交易商對客戶交易占65.9%。這是雙向活動指標，不能證明資金單向買進通膨部位，但確認損益兩平通膨率上升之際，市場正積極轉移通膨風險。

Daly的政策評估，為把這波能源衝擊轉化成立即升息設下很高門檻。她表示，關稅、油價與AI價格衝擊很可能只是暫時性，勞動市場未對通膨形成助力，近期數據也未出現廣泛持續性的新證據。交易員認為9月升息機率約為30%，低於7月底的逾70%。7月就業人數萎縮、核心通膨溫和，以及零售銷售創一年多來最大跌幅，都降低聯準會因單一商品價格波動而採取行動的可能性。她的立場尤其重要，因為這解釋了為何較長天期通膨補償上升時，前端仍然穩定。

Musalem主張的政策反應更為鷹派。他原本會在7月會議升息，並認為若不收緊政策，未來18個月通膨維持在目標以上的機率較高。他的觀點使鷹派陣營擴大至7月投反對票的3名委員之外。同時，他明確表示通膨預期仍穩定，並否認聯準會公信力是長端賣壓的原因。他的診斷結合了兩套原本相互競爭的敘事：若通膨擴散，央行仍可能需要收緊政策；但目前長端殖利率偏高，主要反映政府與AI融資規模，而非市場對貨幣政策的信心脫錨。

AI本身也正成為這場通膨辯論的一部分。聯準會7月會議紀錄在生產力、就業、物價與金融穩定等議題上多次提及這項技術。部分與會者認為目前僅影響若干消費者價格，其他人則認為投資建置已在推高總需求，或即將如此。部分勞工遭到取代，但資料中心建設也在特定地區造成電工、水管工及營建工人短缺。政策制定者另指出，非銀行機構與區域銀行信用的使用增加；若AI預期落空，可能導致股市重定價、消費走弱並使放款機構承壓。同一輪投資週期可能先推高當前需求與融資成本，之後生產力紅利才會擴大供給。

當日股市分化符合這種兩階段機制。大盤與Nasdaq下跌，半導體指數卻在前一週下跌逾5%後上漲0.53%。Walmart銷售不如預期也是S&P下跌因素之一，其股價創2022年以來最大跌幅。晶片業保持韌性，而消費類股及大盤走弱，並非明確的成長訊號。這顯示，即使利率與物價上升壓迫面向家庭的企業，在產生融資需求的經濟領域，資本支出仍可維持強勁。

## AI融資從數十億邁向資產負債表規模

Broadcom擬議融資大幅提高AI信用週期的規模。放款機構正洽談$600億-$700億優先擔保債務，由Broadcom為其中一部分提供保證，另可能加入$300億次順位分層。總借款可能達$1,000億，但協商仍在進行，資金也可能分階段投入。Blackstone與Apollo正洽談參與，特殊目的機構將發債，為Anthropic及其他公司的晶片與基礎設施提供資金。這是一項融資提案，而非已完成的供給；但即使採區間低端，其規模也足以改變市場對未來信用需求，以及銀行或私募資本資產負債表運用的預期。

這項架構把風險由傳統Broadcom公司債轉移至保證、租賃設備及客戶需求構成的鏈條。先前AI XPV合作架構下的一筆$350億交易，由Broadcom為大部分債務提供擔保，Apollo、Blackstone與其他投資人則為租予Anthropic的客製化晶片提供融資。該支撐使優先分層取得投資級評等並降低借款成本。新方案可能在規模大幅擴大的優先層之下加入次順位債。因此，損失保護取決於保證的確切條款、擔保品價值、租賃現金流及專用晶片的剩餘需求，而不能只看Broadcom本身的營運信用。

產能目標說明這不能被視為孤立交易。該合作架構計畫資助超過20吉瓦運算能力，約相當於20座核電廠的輸出，所需資金將達數千億美元。Nvidia另行宣布，包括BlackRock與Goldman Sachs在內的金融機構正為AI基礎設施籌集逾$5,000億。這些數字是未來承諾，並非市場已吸收的債券，但仍改變了前瞻供給問題：對存續期間的競爭正成為可重複運作的平台，而非公司債季節性集中發行。

Broadcom洽談案是AI融資題材的最新增量。先前交易已證明，即使價格要求嚴苛，融資管道仍然暢通：Alphabet已完成的A$55億澳洲交易、QTS規模$39億且殖利率7.228%的Microsoft相關專案融資，以及含夾層融資的$160億Nexus資料中心方案。Broadcom的洽談把潛在單筆規模提高一個數量級，並將設備供應商、AI模型公司與另類資產管理機構納入同一資本結構。財政部每次回購操作的規模為數十億美元；單一AI平台考慮的優先與次順位債務則達數百億美元。

8月20日完成的初級市場交易顯示，一般高評級發行仍然暢通。Vylor在與Corteva分拆前發行$11億5年期與10年期債券，其中10年期券定價為美國公債殖利率加100個基點，初步討論水準約為加135個基點。所得資金將用於向Corteva另一單位EIDP配發，而$14.2億EIDP票據已提交交換為Vylor債務。這項交易把槓桿與母公司配發移入即將獨立的種子事業；定價收緊顯示需求存在，但資金用途與交換機制將決定分拆後債權人的地位。

Thales籌得EUR10億，以協助資助其EUR39億收購海事機器人公司Exail。4年期與8年期分層各占一半，吸引逾EUR25.5億訂單，分別以mid-swaps加45與65個基點定價，均較初步指引收緊32.5個基點。荷姆茲海峽水雷危機推升對水下無人機的需求，將提高主權通膨風險的地緣政治衝擊，連結到國防信用市場的收購融資。該交易預期為A-評等且定價大幅收緊，證明高評級融資管道暢通；但以債務資助策略擴張，也為歐洲存續期間增加另一項資金需求。

對殖利率的需求也掩蓋了銀行資本較脆弱的補償。全球額外第一類資本債殖利率約5.7%，相較之下投資級公司債低於5%，政府債券約3.7%。據報其10日滾動波動率比高評級公司債低75%，對於可能取消票息、贖回時間不確定且承擔第一順位損失的證券而言並不尋常。強勁需求把全球或有可轉換債利差推至200個基點以下，為史上首次，也使BNP Paribas得以用該幣別歷來最低的重設利差發行美元AT1。穩定性來自票息收入與持續資金流入，而非這些工具的資本結構風險已被消除。

這種定價張力也見於美國信用市場。藍籌公司債利差接近美國公債殖利率加80個基點，逼近30年低點；在此水準下，利差擴大約12個基點，就會抵銷一整年的額外收益。同時，絕對殖利率持續吸引買盤，新券定價也較初步指引大幅收緊。信用市場並未關閉融資管道以限縮供給，而是在吸收大量發行的同時，只留下極少利差緩衝來因應盈餘不如預期、保證爭議或AI擔保品重定價。

## 債權人控制權成為下檔風險機制

MBS Group在蓬勃發展的AI領域之外，呈現一宗已落地的損失分配案例。BlackRock旗下HPS與Oaktree將最高$9億債務轉為股權後，取得這家好萊塢製作服務公司的控制權。HPS持有$6億第一順位留置權，Oaktree持有$3億次順位留置權。放款人取得$1億承接債務，並同意再投資$4,000萬，取代原股東Hackman Capital Partners與Affinius Capital。這家服務逾600個娛樂據點的公司得以存續，但既有債務與贊助方股權承擔了重整成本。

這項交易反映製作不動產在疫情干擾、2023年好萊塢罷工、借款成本上升及拍攝放緩後的廣泛低迷。Hackman與Affinius於2019年以$6.5億向Carlyle買下MBS與Manhattan Beach Studios。其投資組合中的其他資產也逐步轉由債權人控制：再融資失敗後，Goldman Sachs接管洛杉磯Radford Studio；Netflix曾洽談以遠低於2021年成交價$18.5億的金額收購；Deutsche Bank則正銷售Television City的$3.375億債務，以及Manhattan Beach Studio的一筆$2.4億票據。問題已不再只是暫時的票息負擔。再融資失敗正把擔保債權轉為所有權，並重設擔保品價值。

針對Mark Walter保險事業的調查，凸顯另一種債權人風險：評等、關係人分類及監理資本是否準確反映支撐保戶權益的資產。聯邦調查人員向Egan-Jones索取其為Walter控制的兩家保險公司Delaware Life與Clear Spring提供服務的紀錄。Egan-Jones表示，公司不是調查對象或目標。Delaware Life與Clear Spring於6月揭露，在2月收到傳票並完成內部檢視後，逾$200億貸款因與Walter或其其他事業有所關聯，應被歸類為關係人交易。

評等集中度使調查具有實質財務意義。截至2025年底，Delaware Life規模$320億的債券投資組合中，約16%只有Egan-Jones一家已知評等機構；Clear Spring規模$63億的投資組合中，至少50%亦是如此。兩家保險公司自2024年以來已向該評等機構支付$800萬。投資級認定可降低保險公司必須持有的監理資本，因此問題不只是揭露用語，還涉及支撐私募且可能缺乏流動性貸款的損失吸收資本規模、獨立價格審查程度，以及與所有人有關聯的交易是否受到關係人曝險應有的監督。

相較先前Sammons Financial及Guggenheim相關債務重定價，本次資訊構成重要更新。新資訊指出檢方索取哪一家外部評等機構的紀錄，並量化兩家Walter控制的保險公司對單一評等機構的依賴程度。這不代表Egan-Jones有不法行為，也不代表標的債券出現損失；但確實顯示，當私募信用在關係企業間移轉時，法律控制權、經濟關聯、評等來源與保險公司資本處理，可能比整體投資級標籤更重要。

肯亞銀行則從相反方向展現對流動性主權債權的偏好。2025年其政府證券持有量增加19%至資產的30%，貸款與墊款則成長6.6%，占8.35兆先令資產負債表的48%。不良貸款比率維持約15%，為東非最高，政府積欠款項也持續使借款人承壓。主權殖利率下降並未吸引銀行增加民間放款；信用品質疲弱使政府債券相對更具用途。這不是美國收盤的驅動因素，但它獨立且重要地說明，當民間信用傳導惡化時，銀行資產負債表可如何強化主權債需求。

## 本地政策訊號不支持單一全球存續期間交易

印度出現本日幅度最大的政策重定價。印度儲備銀行8月3日至5日會議紀錄的鷹派程度明顯高於會後聲明，推升10年期政府公債殖利率盤中最多5個基點至6.87%，5年期殖利率最多8個基點至6.53%。政策委員會此前一致決議將附買回利率維持在5.25%，政策立場為中性。副總裁Poonam Gupta表示，年內可能浮現升息理由；總裁Sanjay Malhotra表示，廣泛物價壓力可能需要收緊政策；外部委員Ram Singh與Saugata Bhattacharya則提出重新校準或迅速調整的可能性。

溝通轉變之所以重要，是因為此前才發生另一項意外：提前結束原本支撐外匯存底及盧比流動性的外幣存款特別誘因。Citigroup將預估啟動緊縮的時間提前至12月，預期累計升息50個基點，若證據擴大，10月也可能行動。Goldman Sachs預期12月與2月各升息25個基點。這些是有明確歸屬的預測，而非已實現政策。目前結論較為有限：交易員在鴿派聲明後累積存續期間部位，會議紀錄揭露更廣泛的升息討論後，隨即反轉中段與短端曝險。

澳洲在最新勞動數據公布後走向相反方向。7月失業率升至4.5%，高於4.4%的市場共識，並創近5年最高；就業人數減少15,800人，而非預期增加12,000人，減幅全數來自兼職工作。澳幣一度下跌0.3%，3年期政府公債殖利率最多下降4個基點，市場定價的12月前升息機率由68%降至62%。澳洲儲備銀行將利率維持在4.35%後，總裁Michele Bullock曾表示再次升息很有可能；RBA也仍認為勞動市場略緊於充分就業水準。這項數據降低再次行動的急迫性，但並未解除央行對通膨上行風險的疑慮。

房市證實澳洲緊縮已在傳導。全國住宅價格較3月高點低2.8%，主要銀行的房貸申請自5月中旬以來約下降10%-15%，6月當季新增投資人貸款減少逾10%，其中新南威爾斯州降幅逾14%。稅制變動正強化RBA今年稍早3次升息的效果。在發行A$170億後，國家總債務一度超過A$1兆，但到期償付預計將使其回落至該門檻以下，且相較其他已開發市場，債務仍低。本週標售投標額近發行量的5倍，AAA評等也維持穩定，使這項里程碑有別於融資警報。

面對同一能源衝擊，瑞典與埃及均選擇謹慎。瑞典央行連續第12個月將政策利率維持在1.75%，符合受訪19名經濟學家一致預期，並重申若夏季通膨轉為持續，2026年稍後仍可能升息。核心通膨小幅上升，但仍明顯低於2%目標，勞動市場則弱於預期。埃及在7月通膨加速至14.9%後，連續第4次會議將存款與放款利率維持在19%與20%。即使月增通膨未變，外部融資包括IMF約$18億及歐盟執委會EUR15億，央行仍因伊朗衝突威脅匯率與燃料進口成本而暫停寬鬆週期。

日本超長債需求尚可、借款成本上升，稍後公布的通膨數據則提供確認。20年期政府公債標售投標倍數略高於1年平均，但低於前次發行；最大幾家國內交易商的需求分布均衡。標售尾差較7月擴大，最低得標價格也低於標售前預估，限制了結果的強度。不過，在美國回購公告帶動下，20年期殖利率仍下降8個基點至3.695%，40年期下降10個基點至4.05%。標售顯示，接近30年高點的殖利率已進入具價值的區間，而非財政疑慮或日本央行正常化已經消失。

海外資金流向與機構債發行顯示日本壓力集中之處。海外投資人7月淨賣出JPY1.28兆2年期與5年期JGB，創2006年7月以來最大流出，因日圓疲弱提高市場對BOJ加速緊縮的預期；但仍買進原始到期期限超過10年的債券JPY8,898億。日本學生支援機構以1.689%票息發行JPY300億債券，創2004年開始發債以來最高，較JGB高1個基點。日本住宅金融支援機構發行JPY103億住宅抵押貸款擔保證券，票息創3.45%新高，使部分房貸利率可能在9月上調。機構債需求強勁，仍未阻止較高主權利率傳導至學生與房屋所有人。

美國收盤後，日本公布7月不含生鮮食品CPI年增1.8%，符合市場共識，並由1.6%加速；不含生鮮食品與能源的指標及整體CPI均上升1.9%。能源成本在6月小幅下降後上升0.6%。數據公布時間太晚，無法解釋8月20日美國公債收盤；但確實進一步支持隨後亞洲交易時段對BOJ近期升息的判斷，先前日圓疲弱及政府傾向在9月或10月採取行動已支撐這項預期。

歐洲主權債分化提醒市場，全球殖利率偏高並不會抹去各地財政公信力差異。2027年大選前，投資人日益接受義大利殖利率低於法國，因總理Giorgia Meloni領導的政府被視為較穩定且致力削減赤字；法國則面臨艱難預算協商，海外持有人占比也較高。義大利主權債僅9%由歐元區外投資人持有，法國則為26%；義大利國內家庭持有14%。即使兩條曲線都面臨相同油價與全球存續期間壓力，持有人結構差異仍可能使政治波動以不同方式傳導。

## 前瞻市場意義

Bessent承諾的財政公告，是檢驗財政部托底能否超越資金流介入的直接測試。若措施能量化且持久地影響赤字與現金借款，回購計畫就會得到基本面支撐，也可防止長端殖利率下一次上升重演週四反轉。若仍只是廣泛訴諸成長、關稅收入或減少詐欺，卻未實質改變預估融資，30年期殖利率將持續對每次標售或公司債供給擴大保持敏感，曲線也可能增加溝通溢價。

週一將公布的伊朗制裁措施，必須從實體能源傳導判斷。若措施實質減少伊朗出口、限制中國採購，或提高航運與保險成本，Brent漲勢將延續，10年期損益兩平通膨率上升4個基點對聯準會條件式緊縮傾向的重要性也會提高。若執法有限或替代流量得以維持，通膨成分將減弱，長端討論會重新聚焦實質期限溢價、赤字及債務供給。若油價上升開始在推高損益兩平通膨率的同時，也帶動2年期殖利率上揚，而非讓前端停在4.19%，核心論點就會出現最大轉變。

Broadcom融資洽談界定AI信用市場下一個定價落點檢驗。關鍵資訊不只有$1,000億的最高名目金額，還包括最終優先與次順位規模、Broadcom保證、擔保品與租賃條款、評等、融資順序，以及銀行或私募資本贊助方保留的金額。若透過強力保證使優先層取得投資級定價，融資管道可維持暢通，但風險將集中於次順位層與贊助方資產負債表。若實際定價明顯擴大、交易縮減或聯貸延後，則顯示資本市場開始配給AI建置資金，而其潛在融資規模如今已可比擬大型主權計畫。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The August 20 U.S. fixed-income close rejected the idea that Treasury buybacks had established a durable ceiling for long yields. The 2-year Treasury yield was unchanged at 4.19%, while the 5-year, 10-year and 30-year yields each rose 4 basis points, to 4.39%, 4.69% and 5.23%. The parallel increase from 5 years outward steepened both 2s10s and 2s30s by 4 basis points, to 50 and 104. That left the long bond only 4 basis points below the level reached before Treasury's surprise intervention on August 19 and 12 basis points higher over 1 month. The policy announcement produced a powerful one-day flow response; the completed next close showed that it had not displaced the fiscal, inflation and competing-supply premiums embedded in duration.

The reversal also changed the composition of the move. The 10-year real yield held at 2.35%, while the 10-year breakeven rose 4 basis points to 2.34%. Brent increased 1.77% to $93.24 and WTI gained 0.51% to $86.27 as President Donald Trump threatened an economic campaign against Iran and its trading partners. Wednesday's rally had been entirely a real-yield event with breakevens unchanged. Thursday's selloff instead reintroduced inflation compensation at the benchmark maturity. Treasury's attempt to reduce privately held duration remains relevant, but an oil shock can still raise the nominal yield even when the real rate does not move.

Two same-day policy signals reinforced the split. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly, a nonvoter in 2026, saw no urgent case for a preemptive hike and said recent inflation and labor readings had not produced the broader persistence she fears. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem, also a nonvoter, reiterated that he would have supported a July increase and assigned greater risk to inflation failing to return to 2% within 18 months without tighter policy. Musalem nevertheless attributed the bond selloff to government financing and AI-related capital demand, not lost Fed credibility. The unchanged 2-year yield shows that neither side forced an immediate repricing of the policy rate. The rise in breakevens and the steeper curve show that patience at the front end does not immunize the long end from energy, deficits or supply.

Cross-asset performance was consistent with a higher nominal discount rate and skepticism about administrative yield relief, not a generalized funding break. The S&P 500 fell 0.87%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.72% for a fifth decline, and the VIX rose 7.52% to 16.01. The Dollar Index was nearly unchanged at 98.796 after its sharp prior-day fall, while gold futures rose 2.07% to $4,582.30. Investment-grade duration absorbed more damage than shorter and lower-quality credit: LQD fell 0.48%, against declines of about 0.19%-0.20% in HYG and JNK. The U.S. government 20-plus-year bond index lost 0.81%, and long high-grade corporate indices fell about 0.85%-0.90%. Those returns reflect duration and total-return pressure rather than a measured cash-spread move.

The most consequential new supply information made Treasury's structural problem larger, not smaller. Broadcom was discussing a special-purpose financing with $60 billion-$70 billion of senior secured debt, a possible $30 billion junior tranche and potential total borrowing of as much as $100 billion to fund AI chips for Anthropic and other users. Treasury can alter the maturity distribution of federal financing at the margin. It cannot prevent highly rated technology sponsors, private-capital firms and AI customers from drawing on the same long-term savings pool. The August 20 close therefore restored the hierarchy that the prior day's rally had temporarily interrupted: energy moved the inflation component, Treasury's communication altered near-term flow, and fiscal plus AI financing still set the burden on real duration.

## The Buyback Put Fails Its First Retest

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent strengthened the verbal commitment behind the buyback program on Thursday even as its market effect faded. He said operations scheduled to begin September 9 could exceed the currently planned $4 billion per issue and described a broader toolkit for supporting orderly markets. He also said the administration would announce an increased focus on fiscal consolidation at the end of the week or early the next, with President Trump assigning Bessent and Budget Director Russ Vought to the effort. No detailed spending, revenue or debt-management measures accompanied those comments. The market therefore received a larger potential intervention and a prospective fiscal initiative, but no new reduction in the underlying borrowing requirement.

That distinction was visible in the path of the 30-year yield. It rose as much as 7 basis points intraday to 5.27%, briefly moving above its pre-announcement area, before closing at 5.23%. Bessent's comments helped pare the selloff, showing that the official reaction function still carries tactical force. Yet the close recaptured most of Wednesday's 9-basis-point decline. The 10-year similarly ended at 4.69%, 4 basis points higher. A policy signal can induce short covering and reduce expected net duration around scheduled operations; sustaining a lower equilibrium yield requires either a larger change in auction supply or a credible improvement in inflation, growth or fiscal cash flows.

The buyback amount remains modest against both the market and the government's financing gap. Treasury's tentative September 9-November 4 calendar had allowed as much as $14 billion of purchases in the 10- to 30-year sector, so a doubling implies at least $14 billion of additional demand. JPMorgan estimates a funding gap of more than $3.5 trillion in coming fiscal years and points to a budget deficit near 6% of GDP in an economy operating close to full employment. Total public debt has crossed $40 trillion. Bessent argued that tariff revenue, economic growth and fraud reduction could improve the trajectory and said there was a good chance the deficit had peaked. The promised fiscal package will need to turn those broad channels into measures large enough to change projected cash borrowing; otherwise the buyback merely rearranges part of the maturity supply.

Financing the purchases also redistributes rather than removes interest-rate risk. Treasury commonly uses bills for fluctuating funding needs, so retiring or holding more long-dated off-the-run securities can be paired with additional short-term issuance. That reduces the duration absorbed by private investors today but increases refinancing frequency and leaves the deficit intact. It also complicates the meaning of the long yield. A lower 30-year rate caused by official maturity management is not the same signal about inflation, fiscal sustainability or prospective nominal growth as a rally caused by weaker data.

The communication cost became more concrete after the reversal. Treasury had released its regular quarterly borrowing strategy only two weeks before unexpectedly changing buyback sizes. Strategists at JPMorgan and Jefferies and investors at PGIM warned that departing from a regular and predictable process could increase the term premium investors require. PGIM co-CIO Greg Peters, a member of the Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee, estimated that the announcement lowered the government's cost on the $16 billion 20-year auction by roughly $200 million. The auction itself drew tepid demand even after 20-year yields had fallen. A tactical saving on one sale can coexist with a higher structural premium if investors become less certain about future auction sizes, buyback schedules and the political threshold for intervention.

Cash activity did not suggest a disorderly market requiring emergency support. Treasury trading totaled $1.246 trillion in original-face par value, 9.0% below the prior session, and nominal coupon activity was $1.016 trillion, down 8.6%. More than 20-year securities still recorded $137.9 billion of activity across 50,919 trades, with dealer-to-customer transactions representing 47.2% of par value. Turnover was 19.2% below Wednesday's buyback-driven surge. The reversal occurred in an active, two-way market rather than through a collapse in transactions. Treasury's stated liquidity purpose may improve off-the-run functioning, but the day's price action was a disagreement over value and policy durability.

The dollar supplied another boundary around the intervention. It did not extend Wednesday's 0.8% decline, ending almost flat, even as Citi cut its 3-month Dollar Index forecast to 98.34 from 102.12. Citi argued that buybacks weaken the currency through lower U.S. yields and concern about financial repression, and raised its 3-month EUR/USD forecast to 1.1750. Other investors similarly identified the dollar as the potential relief valve if authorities suppress term yields without improving fiscal credibility. Thursday's stable close shows that this transmission is not automatic. Higher oil prices, U.S. AI-related capital inflows and the rebound in yields all supported the currency. Over a longer horizon, repeated intervention without fiscal delivery could still move the risk premium from bonds into foreign exchange and gold rather than eliminate it.

The institutional tension reaches the Fed as well. Chair Kevin Warsh has asked investors to take their lead from economic data and form their own market prices, but Treasury is now explicitly signaling that long yields do not reflect fundamentals. If buybacks materially ease mortgage, corporate and financial conditions during above-target inflation, the Fed may need to decide whether that easing reduces the restraint it intended to obtain from market rates. If the operations remain too small to affect conditions, they add noise without changing the policy requirement. Thursday's reversal favored the latter interpretation, but the larger announced toolkit keeps the issue alive.

## Oil Reopens the Inflation Side of the Curve

Energy was the clearest current change in the rates mix. Brent's rise to $93.24 extended its 1-week gain to 7.09%, while the 10-year breakeven reached 2.34%, 10 basis points higher over the same period. Trump said the United States would wage economic warfare against Iran and promised details at a Monday press conference, including pressure on countries, banks and businesses that maintain economic ties with Tehran. China is the dominant buyer of Iranian oil, making the threat potentially broader than a bilateral sanctions escalation. No measures had yet been specified by the close, but the prospect of tighter enforcement reduced confidence that the existing workarounds around disrupted Gulf flows would continue unchanged.

The move was not a simple repeat of the earlier oil shock. On August 19, the 10-year nominal yield fell 6 basis points because the real yield dropped by the same amount, while breakeven inflation held at 2.30%. On August 20, the real yield remained at 2.35% and the breakeven supplied the entire 4-basis-point rise in the nominal benchmark. That reversal says the market separated Treasury's duration intervention from the physical inflation channel within one session. Buybacks can remove some long bonds from dealer inventories or investor portfolios; they do not create crude supply, lower shipping insurance costs or resolve the U.S.-Iran conflict.

The inflation move remained contained rather than systemic. The 2-year yield did not rise, the Dollar Index was stable, and the VIX closed at 16.01 rather than signaling broad funding stress. WTI's 0.51% increase was much smaller than Brent's, indicating a geographically uneven shock rather than a uniform surge in all crude benchmarks. TIPS trading did become more prominent: $36.7 billion of par value changed hands, 25.7% more than the prior day, with dealer-to-customer activity accounting for 65.9%. That is a two-way activity measure, not evidence of directional inflation buying, but it confirms that the market was actively transferring inflation risk as breakevens rose.

Daly's policy assessment places a high threshold on converting this energy impulse into an immediate rate increase. She said tariff, oil and AI price shocks were likely to be temporary, saw no labor-market contribution to inflation and found no new evidence of broad persistence in recent releases. Traders assigned about a 30% chance to a September hike, down from more than 70% at the end of July. July payroll contraction, subdued core inflation and the largest retail-sales decline in more than a year have made the Fed less likely to react to a single commodity move. Her stance is especially relevant because it explains why the front end stayed anchored as inflation compensation rose farther out.

Musalem described a less forgiving reaction function. He would have raised rates at the July meeting and sees a greater chance that inflation remains above target over the next 18 months without tighter policy. His view expands the hawkish coalition beyond the three July voters who dissented. At the same time, he explicitly said inflation expectations remain anchored and rejected Fed credibility as the cause of the long-end selloff. His diagnosis joins two otherwise competing stories: the central bank may still need to tighten if inflation broadens, but today's high long yields principally reflect the quantity of government and AI financing rather than a de-anchoring of faith in monetary policy.

AI itself is becoming part of that inflation debate. July Fed minutes referred repeatedly to the technology across productivity, employment, prices and financial stability. Several participants saw only selected consumer-price effects so far, while others thought the investment build-out was already raising aggregate demand or soon would. Some workers are being displaced, yet data-center construction is creating shortages of electricians, plumbers and construction workers in particular regions. Policymakers also noted the increasing use of nonbank and regional-bank credit and the risk that disappointed AI expectations could reprice equities, weaken consumption and strain lenders. The same investment cycle can raise current demand and financing costs before any productivity dividend expands supply.

The session's equity split fitted that two-stage mechanism. The broad market and Nasdaq fell, yet the semiconductor index gained 0.53% after losing more than 5% over the prior week. Walmart's disappointing sales contributed to the S&P decline, and its shares suffered their largest fall since 2022. A resilient chip sector alongside weak consumer and broad equity performance is not a clean growth signal. It shows that capital spending can remain strong in the part of the economy generating financing demand even as higher rates and prices pressure household-facing businesses.

## AI Finance Moves From Billions to Balance-Sheet Scale

Broadcom's proposed financing materially raises the scale of the AI credit cycle. Lenders were discussing $60 billion-$70 billion of senior secured debt, with Broadcom guaranteeing a portion, plus a possible $30 billion junior tranche. Total borrowing could reach $100 billion, although negotiations were continuing and the capital might be deployed incrementally. Blackstone and Apollo were in talks to participate, and a special-purpose vehicle would issue the debt to finance chips and infrastructure for Anthropic and other companies. This is a financing proposal rather than completed supply, but even its lower range is large enough to alter expectations for future credit demand and bank or private-capital balance-sheet use.

The structure moves risk away from a conventional Broadcom corporate bond and into a chain of guarantees, leased equipment and customer demand. An earlier $35 billion transaction under the AI XPV partnership had Broadcom backstop most of the debt while Apollo, Blackstone and other investors financed custom chips leased to Anthropic. That support allowed senior tranches to obtain investment-grade ratings and lower borrowing costs. The new plan could add junior debt beneath a much larger senior layer. Loss protection therefore depends on the exact guarantee, collateral value, lease cash flows and residual demand for specialized chips, not simply Broadcom's operating credit.

The capacity target shows why the financing cannot be treated as an isolated transaction. The partnership aims to fund more than 20 gigawatts of computing power, roughly the output of 20 nuclear plants, and will require hundreds of billions of dollars. Nvidia separately announced that financial firms including BlackRock and Goldman Sachs were assembling more than $500 billion for AI infrastructure. Those figures are prospective commitments, not bonds already absorbed by the market. They still change the forward supply question: the competition for duration is becoming a repeatable platform rather than a seasonal burst of corporate issuance.

This development is the current delta to the AI funding story. Prior transactions had already established strong access at demanding prices: Alphabet's completed A$5.5 billion Australian deal, QTS's $3.9 billion Microsoft-linked project financing at 7.228%, and the $16 billion Nexus data-center package with a mezzanine layer. Broadcom's discussions increase the possible unit size by an order of magnitude and move equipment vendors, AI model companies and alternative-asset managers into one capital structure. The Treasury's buyback operations are measured in several billions per event. One AI platform is contemplating tens of billions in senior and junior debt.

Completed primary deals on August 20 showed that ordinary high-grade issuance remained open. Vylor sold $1.1 billion of 5- and 10-year bonds ahead of its separation from Corteva, with the 10-year pricing at 100 basis points over Treasuries after initial discussion near 135 basis points. Proceeds will fund a distribution to another Corteva unit, EIDP, while $1.42 billion of EIDP notes had been tendered for exchange into Vylor debt. The transaction transfers leverage and a parent payout into the soon-to-be independent seed business; the tighter execution shows demand, but the use of proceeds and exchange mechanics determine the post-separation creditor position.

Thales raised EUR1 billion to help finance its EUR3.9 billion acquisition of maritime robotics company Exail. The evenly split 4- and 8-year tranches attracted more than EUR2.55 billion of orders and priced at 45 and 65 basis points over mid-swaps, both 32.5 basis points tighter than initial indications. Demand for submarine drones has increased amid the Strait of Hormuz mine crisis, linking the geopolitical shock that raises sovereign inflation risk to acquisition financing in defense credit. The deal's expected A- rating and strong tightening demonstrate high-grade access, yet the use of debt to fund strategic expansion adds another claim on European duration.

Yield demand is also masking more fragile compensation in bank capital. Global additional Tier 1 debt yielded about 5.7%, compared with less than 5% for investment-grade corporates and about 3.7% for government bonds. Its rolling 10-day volatility was reported at 75% below that of high-grade corporate debt, an unusual result for securities exposed to coupon cancellation, uncertain calls and first-loss absorption. Strong demand pushed global contingent-convertible spreads below 200 basis points for the first time and allowed BNP Paribas to issue a dollar AT1 at its tightest reset spread in that currency. Stability is being generated by coupon income and persistent inflows, not by removal of the instruments' capital-structure risks.

That pricing tension is visible across U.S. credit. Blue-chip corporate spreads were near 80 basis points over Treasuries, close to a three-decade low, and a widening of roughly 12 basis points would erase a year of incremental income at that level. At the same time, absolute yields continue to attract buyers and new deals tighten sharply from initial guidance. The market is not rationing credit by closing. It is accepting large supply while leaving little spread cushion for an earnings disappointment, a guarantee dispute or a repricing of AI collateral.

## Creditor Control Becomes the Downside Mechanism

MBS Group supplied a realized loss-allocation event outside the booming AI complex. BlackRock's HPS and Oaktree took control of the Hollywood production-services company after converting as much as $900 million of debt into equity. HPS held a $600 million first lien and Oaktree a $300 million junior lien. The lenders received $100 million of take-back debt and agreed to invest another $40 million, displacing owners Hackman Capital Partners and Affinius Capital. A company serving more than 600 entertainment locations survived, but legacy debt and sponsor equity absorbed the restructuring cost.

The transaction reflects a broader downturn in production property after pandemic disruption, the 2023 Hollywood strikes, higher borrowing costs and slower filming. Hackman and Affinius had paid Carlyle $650 million for MBS and Manhattan Beach Studios in 2019. Other assets in their portfolio have moved toward creditor control: Goldman Sachs seized Los Angeles's Radford Studio after refinancing failed, Netflix has discussed buying it for a fraction of the $1.85 billion paid in 2021, and Deutsche Bank is marketing $337.5 million of Television City debt plus a $240 million note on Manhattan Beach Studio. The mechanism is no longer a temporary coupon burden. Refinancing failure is converting secured claims into ownership and resetting collateral values.

The investigation around Mark Walter's insurance businesses raises a different form of creditor risk: whether ratings, related-party classification and regulatory capital accurately describe the assets supporting policyholders. Federal investigators sought records from Egan-Jones concerning its work for Delaware Life and Clear Spring, two Walter-controlled insurers. Egan-Jones said it was not a subject or target of the investigation. Delaware Life and Clear Spring disclosed in June that more than $20 billion of loans should have been classified as affiliated transactions because of links to Walter or his other businesses, following a February subpoena and internal review.

Rating concentration makes the inquiry financially material. Egan-Jones was the sole known rating provider for about 16% of Delaware Life's $32 billion bond portfolio at the end of 2025 and at least 50% of Clear Spring's $6.3 billion book. The two insurers have paid the rater $8 million since 2024. An investment-grade designation can reduce the regulatory capital an insurer must hold, so the issue is not only disclosure language. It reaches the amount of loss-absorbing capital behind private and potentially illiquid loans, the degree of independent price scrutiny and whether transactions connected to an owner received the oversight expected for affiliated exposure.

This is a material update to the earlier repricing of Sammons Financial and Guggenheim-linked debt. The new information identifies the outside rating records sought by prosecutors and quantifies how heavily two Walter-controlled insurers relied on one rater. It does not establish wrongdoing by Egan-Jones or a loss on the underlying bonds. It does show why legal control, economic affiliation, rating provenance and insurer capital treatment can matter more than an aggregate investment-grade label when private credit moves across related entities.

Kenyan banks show the same preference for liquid sovereign claims from the opposite direction. Their government-security holdings rose 19% in 2025 to 30% of assets, while loans and advances grew 6.6% and represented 48% of an 8.35 trillion-shilling balance sheet. Nonperforming loans remained near 15%, the highest ratio in East Africa, and state arrears continued to pressure borrowers. Falling sovereign yields did not draw banks toward more private lending; weak credit quality made government bonds comparatively useful. This is not a driver of the U.S. close, but it is an independently important example of how bank balance sheets can reinforce sovereign demand when private-credit transmission deteriorates.

## Local Policy Signals Resist a Single Global Duration Trade

India delivered the sharpest realized policy repricing. Minutes from the Reserve Bank of India's August 3-5 meeting were markedly more hawkish than the accompanying statement, sending the 10-year government yield as much as 5 basis points higher to 6.87% and the 5-year as much as 8 basis points higher to 6.53%. The policy committee had unanimously held the repo rate at 5.25% with a neutral stance. Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said a case for a hike could emerge during the year, Governor Sanjay Malhotra said broad-based price pressure might require tighter policy, and external members Ram Singh and Saugata Bhattacharya raised the possibility of recalibration or swift adjustment.

The communication shift matters because it followed another surprise: the early closure of a special foreign-currency deposit incentive that had supported reserves and rupee liquidity. Citigroup brought forward its projected start of tightening to December and expects 50 basis points of cumulative increases, with October described as live if evidence broadens. Goldman Sachs expects quarter-point moves in December and February. Those are attributable forecasts, not realized policy. The current conclusion is narrower: traders had accumulated duration after a dovish statement and then reversed both belly and short-end exposure when the minutes disclosed a wider tightening discussion.

Australia moved in the opposite direction after a fresh labor release. July unemployment rose to 4.5%, above the 4.4% consensus and the highest in nearly five years, while employment fell by 15,800 instead of increasing by the expected 12,000. The loss came entirely from part-time jobs. The Australian dollar fell as much as 0.3%, the 3-year government yield declined as much as 4 basis points, and market pricing for an increase by December fell to 62% from 68%. Governor Michele Bullock had said another hike was quite possible after the Reserve Bank held at 4.35%, and the RBA still viewed labor conditions as somewhat tighter than full employment. The data reduce the urgency of another move without resolving the central bank's concern about upside inflation.

Housing confirms that Australian restraint is already transmitting. National dwelling prices were 2.8% below their March peak, mortgage applications at the major banks had fallen roughly 10%-15% since mid-May, and new investor loans dropped more than 10% in the June quarter, including more than 14% in New South Wales. Tax changes are reinforcing the effect of three RBA increases earlier in the year. Gross national debt temporarily exceeded A$1 trillion after A$17 billion of issuance, though maturities were set to take it back below that threshold and debt remains low relative to developed-market peers. Nearly five times as many bids as bonds offered at the week's sale and stable AAA ratings distinguish the milestone from a funding alarm.

Sweden and Egypt chose caution under the same energy shock. The Riksbank held its policy rate at 1.75% for a twelfth month, as all 19 surveyed economists expected, and repeated that an increase later in 2026 remained possible if summer inflation became persistent. Core inflation had edged higher but remained clearly below the 2% target, while the labor market was weaker than expected. Egypt held its deposit and lending rates at 19% and 20% for a fourth meeting after July inflation accelerated to 14.9%. The central bank has paused an easing cycle because the Iran conflict threatens its currency and fuel-import bill, even though monthly inflation was unchanged and external financing included about $1.8 billion from the IMF and EUR1.5 billion from the European Commission.

Japan combined adequate superlong demand with rising borrowing costs and a later inflation confirmation. The 20-year government auction posted a bid-to-cover ratio marginally above its 1-year average, though below the previous sale, and demand was evenly distributed among the largest domestic dealers. The tail widened from July and the lowest accepted price was below pre-auction estimates, limiting the strength of the result. The 20-year yield nevertheless fell 8 basis points to 3.695%, and the 40-year dropped 10 basis points to 4.05%, helped by the U.S. buyback announcement. The sale showed that yields near three-decade highs had reached a value zone, not that fiscal concern or Bank of Japan normalization had disappeared.

Foreign flows and agency issuance show where Japanese pressure is concentrated. Overseas investors sold a net JPY1.28 trillion of 2- and 5-year JGBs in July, the largest outflow since July 2006, as yen weakness increased expectations of faster BOJ tightening. They still bought JPY889.8 billion of bonds with original maturities beyond 10 years. Japan Student Services Organization sold JPY30 billion of bonds at a 1.689% coupon, its highest since issuance began in 2004 and 1 basis point over JGBs. Japan Housing Finance Agency set a record 3.45% coupon on JPY10.3 billion of residential mortgage-backed securities, raising the prospect that some mortgage rates increase in September. Strong agency demand did not prevent higher sovereign rates from reaching students and homeowners.

After the U.S. close, Japan's July CPI excluding fresh food was released at 1.8% year on year, matching consensus and accelerating from 1.6%; the measure excluding fresh food and energy and the overall CPI both rose 1.9%. Energy costs increased 0.6% after a slight June decline. The release occurred too late to explain the August 20 Treasury close. It does reinforce the subsequent Asian-session case for a near-term BOJ increase, which had already been supported by yen weakness and a government preference for action in September or October.

European sovereign differentiation remains a reminder that high global yields do not erase local fiscal credibility. Investors have increasingly accepted lower Italian yields than French yields ahead of 2027 elections because Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government is viewed as more stable and committed to deficit reduction, while France faces difficult budget negotiations and a larger foreign holder base. Only 9% of Italian sovereign bonds are held outside the euro area, compared with 26% for France, and domestic Italian households hold 14%. Those ownership differences can make political volatility transmit differently even when both curves face the same oil and global-duration pressure.

## Forward Market Significance

Bessent's promised fiscal announcement is the direct test of whether the Treasury put can become more than a flow intervention. Measures with quantified and durable effects on the deficit and cash borrowing would give the buyback program a fundamental counterpart and could keep the next rise in long yields from recreating Thursday's reversal. Another broad appeal to growth, tariff revenue or fraud reduction, without a material change in projected financing, would leave the 30-year yield sensitive to each expansion of auction or corporate supply and could add a communication premium to the curve.

The Iran sanctions announcement due Monday must be judged through physical energy transmission. Measures that materially reduce Iranian exports, constrain Chinese purchases or raise shipping and insurance costs would extend the rise in Brent and make the 10-year breakeven's 4-basis-point increase more relevant to the Fed's conditional tightening bias. Limited enforcement or sustained alternative flows would reduce the inflation component and return the long-end debate toward real term premium, deficits and debt supply. The thesis changes most if higher oil begins lifting the 2-year yield alongside breakevens rather than leaving the front end at 4.19%.

Broadcom's financing discussions define the next clearing-price test for AI credit. The decisive information is not the headline maximum of $100 billion alone, but the final senior and junior sizes, Broadcom's guarantee, collateral and lease terms, ratings, funding sequence and the amount retained by banks or private-capital sponsors. A structure that achieves investment-grade senior pricing through a strong guarantee would preserve access while concentrating risk in the junior layer and sponsor balance sheets. Materially wider execution, a reduced deal or delayed syndication would show that the capital market is beginning to ration an AI build-out whose prospective financing scale now rivals major sovereign programs.
